name: Kitchen Door Frame Repair Steps: How Contractors Align and Restore Racked Jambs

step.name: Step 1: Inspect the jamb opening and check diagonal squareness
step.text: Examine the door frame for loose fasteners, soft spots near the floor, and rubbing marks along the stop. Measure diagonally from top corner to bottom corner in both directions; equal diagonal lengths indicate a square opening, while mismatched numbers reveal frame racking.

step.name: Step 2: Remove hardware and inspect framing clearances
step.text: Take down the door slab and hinge plates to inspect how the jamb sits against the wall studs. Check the jamb depth, thickness, and reveal spacing around the perimeter to understand where binding or bowing is taking place.

step.name: Step 3: Adjust hinge anchoring and position cedar shims
step.text: Replace short factory hinge screws with longer wood screws driven into the wall framing behind the jamb. Insert tapered wood shims behind the hinge and strike locations to correct plumb and eliminate unwanted hollow space.

step.name: Step 4: Splice or replace damaged jamb sections
step.text: If the bottom of the frame has softened from kitchen floor cleaning moisture or spills, cut away the compromised section cleanly. Measure and fit a matching wood jamb piece, fasten it securely, and ensure proper depth alignment with existing trim.

step.name: Step 5: Rehang the door and apply protective sealant
step.text: Rehang the door slab to verify smooth swing and latch engagement. Seal all cut edges, joints, and exposed wood at the base of the frame with high-quality primer and paint to protect against future indoor moisture. When door frames show heavy racking, dry rot, or cracks spreading across surrounding drywall, calling a professional finish contractor ensures the opening is rebuilt correctly.
